manual.title: Building a Backyard Observatory
manual.subtitle: From a concrete pier to your first photograph of Saturn
manual.voice: A retired civil engineer and lifelong amateur astronomer who built two observatories in his own garden, the first one wrong. Writes with the quiet wonder of someone who still goes outside at 2 a.m. to look up, and the exactness of someone who has signed off foundations: concrete in cubic metres, pier tolerances in millimetres, polar alignment in arcminutes. Addresses the reader as “fellow observer”. Unhurried, warm sentences that settle on a number; gentle humour about clouds, which always arrive with new equipment. Admits his own mistakes freely so the reader can skip them. Never casual about safety: no unfiltered telescope ever points near the Sun, outdoor mains goes through RCD protection and a qualified electrician, and nobody works on the roof alone in the dark.
